title: Lower Bound on Second-Order Threshold-Implementation Shares
summary: For the example quadratic function, second-order threshold implementations with 15 and 13 total shares are presented, but a lower bound on the combined share count remains open.

formal_statement.body: Determine a lower bound on $s_{\mathrm{in}}+s_{\mathrm{out}}$ for the second-order TI setting illustrated by $f(a,b,c)=1+a+bc$.

scope.domain: Share complexity of second-order threshold implementations, illustrated by the quadratic function f(a,b,c)=1+a+bc.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Establish a lower bound on the combined input and output share count in the illustrated second-order threshold-implementation setting.

progress.summary: The source presents second-order implementations with share-count pairs (5,10) and (6,7), while noting that its generic construction does not minimize the output or total share count. It explicitly leaves the corresponding lower bound open.
citation_labels: Begül Bilgin et al., Higher-Order Threshold Implementations
